business_problem: Hyperparameter Technology needed huge elastic compute for game-AI training, low-latency global deployment for live gameplay, and a better way to coordinate fast-changing resources across many countries and workload types.
solution_summary: Hyperparameter Technology runs its AI Bot SaaS business on Tencent Cloud so it can train, deploy, and scale game AI globally without carrying fixed infrastructure overhead. The company uses a cloud-native architecture compatible with native Kubernetes, which means teams can load container images without managing cluster nodes while still maximizing cloud-server compute capacity. Tencent's large resource pool and spot instances reduce the cost of deep-learning training for increasingly diverse and independent AI Bots, and the platform can scale as the company moves from simple bot behavior to large populations of interacting agents. For live gameplay, Tencent's global footprint and customized BGP networking place compute near users, find nodes within 30 ms, and optimize routing during overseas congestion peaks. The result is a low-latency AI operations platform that supports very high peak concurrency across dozens of countries.

data_flow: Training jobs and runtime AI Bot services are packaged into Kubernetes-compatible containers and scheduled on elastic cloud servers and spot instances; global network routing then places gameplay close to users and keeps latency low during live interactions.
business_outcome: Tencent Cloud helped Hyperparameter Technology scale AI Bot services to global reach, lower training cost, and keep live interactions responsive even as bot populations and user coverage grew rapidly.
